vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: nm-abstract-hook-authoring
Version: 1.8.2

The skill bundle is a comprehensive educational guide and documentation set for authoring hooks in Claude Code and the Claude Agent SDK. It provides detailed instructions, implementation patterns (Python, JSON, Bash), and best practices for validation, logging, and performance optimization. The content emphasizes security-first design, such as sanitizing logs to prevent secret exposure and implementing fail-safe defaults. No malicious logic, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injections were identified; all code snippets serve as illustrative examples for legitimate developer workflows.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only, security-minded guide for writing Claude Code/Agent hooks and its requests and examples are consistent with that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description describe hook authoring; the SKILL.md and module files exclusively provide hook types, JSON/Python examples, performance/security guidance, and scope guidance. There are no unrelated environment variables, binaries, or install steps requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions legitimately show how to run command-type hooks, write audit logs, perform validation, and POST hook payloads to HTTP endpoints. This is expected for a hook-authoring guide, but the examples grant the operator the ability to execute arbitrary shell commands and send hook JSON to arbitrary URLs — which can be abused if misconfigured. The doc does not instruct reading secrets from unrelated system paths, but examples do reference env checks (e.g., PRODUCTION_APPROVED) and writing to ~/.claude/audit.log; users should audit any concrete hook files before enabling them.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec, no code files to execute, and no downloads. Low risk from installation mechanics.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials. Example code references environment checks (PRODUCTION_APPROVED, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON) and uses home paths like ~/.claude — these are reasonable examples for hook behavior but are not required by the skill itself. Be cautious: hooks you author using these patterns can read environment variables and files, so granting hooks global scope / enabling plugin hooks has privilege implications.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not forced-always and does not request persistent platform privileges. It documents global/project/plugin hook scopes (including global hooks that persist at ~/.claude/settings.json), which is standard. Note that hooks (when enabled) can run autonomously per platform defaults — this is expected behavior for hook code.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This is a coherent, security-focused authoring guide — it contains realistic examples for validation, logging, and policy enforcement. Before installing or enabling any hook you or a plugin provides: 1) review the concrete hook JSON or scripts (they can run arbitrary shell commands or POST to URLs); 2) avoid logging raw tool inputs/outputs that may contain secrets and prefer sanitized/audited logging; 3) prefer project-scoped hooks and code-reviewed plugin hooks over global hooks for sensitive policies; 4) whitelist trusted HTTP endpoints if using HTTP-type hooks; and 5) test hooks in a safe/unprivileged environment (and use workspace trust and permission prompts) to ensure they don't inadvertently read or exfiltrate secrets.
